title: PreSto: An In-Storage Data Preprocessing System for Training Recommendation Models
problem: CPU-centric preprocessing for recommendation systems is bottlenecked on feature generation and feature normalization operations, failing to exploit abundant inter- and intra-feature parallelism. This requires large CPU server fleets, incurring substantial deployment cost and power consumption.
motivation: Efficient preprocessing is critical for sustaining high training throughput in recommendation systems while minimizing deployment cost and energy consumption.
method: PreSto is a storage-centric preprocessing system that leverages In-Storage Processing (ISP) units to offload bottlenecked preprocessing operations (feature generation and normalization) from CPUs. The ISP units exploit inter- and intra-feature parallelism to preprocess raw data and seamlessly feed it to GPUs for training.
key_novelty: Using In-Storage Processing (ISP) units to offload recommendation system preprocessing operations that are bottlenecked in traditional CPU-centric approaches.
contributions: Storage-centric preprocessing system using In-Storage Processing to replace CPU-centric approaches
Characterization of CPU bottlenecks in feature generation and normalization for RecSys preprocessing
ISP system design exploiting inter- and intra-feature parallelism
9.6× speedup, 4.3× cost-efficiency, and 11.3× energy-efficiency improvements over CPU baseline
